 Texas counties break first day early voting records
 BY 
 John Salazar 
 Texas 
 PUBLISHED 9:58 AM CT Oct. 21, 2026 
 PUBLISHED October 21, 2026 @9:58 AM 
 SHARE 
 TEXAS — The five most populous counties in Texas smashed first-day early voting records, surpassing some historic voter numbers set during President Donald Trump’s last midterm elections in 2018.
 Bexar, Dallas, Harris, Tarrant and Travis counties all pushed past early voting records for at least two of the last three elections, according to voter rolls.
 Across the nation’s second most populous state, lengthy polling lines were seen throughout the day Monday.
 In Houston, election workers counted 40,000 more votes than the 2018 record. Voters cast 105,000 ballots on the first day of early voting in Harris County.
 In Dallas County, 76,000 cast their ballots, beating the 2018 midterm record of 59,000, according to Dallas County Judge Clay Jenkins.
 In Bexar County, more than 42,000 showed up to vote — the county’s highest first-day turnout for a midterm election or non-presidential election.
 The same high voter turnout is occurring at polling sites in the Rio Grande Valley in far South Texas.
 Across the greater Rio Grande Valley, 30,000 people voted, according to county numbers.
 The largest county in the RGV, Hidalgo County, saw an increase of almost 50% compared with the 2022 midterm elections.
 In Travis County, home to the state capital of Austin, nearly 41,000 people cast ballots, breaking 2018 and 2022 records, according to the county clerk.
 Turnout was also high in some counties where Trump was more popular in previous elections.
 In Tarrant County, 50,000 voters cast ballots. That represented a 20% increase in voter turnout from 2018.
 Trump won Tarrant County by five points in 2024. Early voting in Texas continues through Oct. 30, and Election Day is Nov. 3.
